answer: A distance-bounding protocol resists Sybil attacks by verifying an agent's physical coordinates using multi-lateration. The node must return a challenge echo within speed-of-light latency thresholds, authenticating devices managing a harbor jetty or freight wharf. An attacker incurs the scarce physical cost of operating distinct, geographically separated radio transceivers per identity. However, this requires dedicated anchor hardware and remains susceptible to directional relay tunnels.
